title: Weighted category gradebook
instructions:
Implement `weighted_mean(pairs)` and `Gradebook` in `gradebook.py`. Numeric inputs are finite real numbers, never booleans; category names are strings. No rounding is performed.
- `weighted_mean(pairs) -> float | None`: consume an iterable of `(value, weight)` pairs. Return sum(value*weight)/sum(weight); return `None` for no pairs. Any weight <= 0 raises `ValueError`.
- `Gradebook(weights)`: take a nonempty dict mapping category names to positive weights; otherwise raise `ValueError`. Copy the mapping so later caller changes do not affect the book.
- `add(category, score, possible=100) -> None`: record one assignment. Unknown category raises `KeyError`. Require possible > 0 and 0 <= score <= possible, else `ValueError`, without changing records.
- `category_average(category) -> float | None`: arithmetic mean of assignment percentages (`100 * score / possible`), not a pooled points ratio. Empty category returns `None`; unknown category raises `KeyError`.
- `overall() -> float | None`: weighted mean of averages of nonempty categories, using their configured weights. Empty categories do not contribute to the denominator. Return `None` if there are no assignments.
- `drop_lowest(category, count=1) -> list[tuple]`: permanently remove up to count assignments with the lowest percentage, ties in insertion order. Return removed `(score, possible)` tuples in selection order (percentage ascending, insertion order for ties). Count is an integer; a negative count raises `ValueError`. Zero removes nothing; a count larger than the category size removes all. Unknown category raises `KeyError` before checking count.
- `report() -> dict`: return a fresh mapping of every category to its average, including `None` for empty categories; preserve the supplied category order. Changes to this mapping do not affect the book.

## Files
- `gradebook.py`
